title: Career Roadmap · Freight Forwarder
summary: A Freight Forwarder coordinates the transportation of goods from exporters to importers by arranging shipping, managing documentation, coordinating customs-related processes and tracking shipments.

about.label: Industry
about.text: International Trade, Shipping, Logistics and Supply Chain Management

about.label: Typical entry route
about.text: Logistics Trainee → Freight Operations Executive → Freight Forwarder

about.label: Work environment
about.text: Freight forwarding companies, shipping agencies, customs brokerage firms, logistics providers and export-import companies

about.label: Career type
about.text: Shipment coordination, international transportation, documentation, customs coordination and customer service

blocks.text: A Freight Forwarder coordinates the transportation of goods from exporters to importers by arranging shipping, managing documentation, coordinating customs-related processes and tracking shipments.

Freight forwarders work with shipping lines, airlines, trucking companies, ports, warehouses, customs brokers and customers. They may coordinate ocean freight, air freight, road transportation or multimodal shipments.

items.text: Obtaining freight quotations and comparing transport options.
Coordinating cargo pickup, port handling and final delivery.
Tracking shipments and communicating status updates.
Coordinating with customs brokers and relevant authorities.
Managing delays, missing documents and cargo discrepancies.
Reviewing freight invoices and shipment-related costs.
Supporting cargo insurance arrangements when requested.
Maintaining customer relationships and coordinating repeat shipments.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Freight forwarding is different from working as a deck or marine engineering officer aboard a ship. This is primarily a logistics and commercial career, and a sea-going officer qualification is not universally required.

These rules help allocate specified costs, responsibilities and risks between buyers and sellers. They do not replace the full sales contract or automatically settle every customs, tax or payment obligation. Use the current official ICC guidance for detailed interpretations.

blocks.text: The strongest candidates combine documentation accuracy, commercial awareness, customer communication, shipment coordination and problem-solving. The key is to understand how goods move from origin to destination and how to manage the paperwork, costs, risks and exceptions throughout the journey.
